entries.EN:
An armored personnel carrier used by army detachments in the Zone for patrols in high risk areas. Features strengthened armor, thermal optic sights with an image identification module, electronic aiming and barrel stabilization systems. The hull has been made airtight for operations in hazardous environments with all analogue controls being replaced with actuator systems. The APC is fully operable by a single person and allows precise fire to be carried on by means of an integrated gun. In the back is ample room for transport of a large squad of troops.

Also known as the "Aleko", the 2141 was a front-wheel drive hatchback with improved features compared to previous Moskvitch models, developed with the help of French engineers and intended to compete with European and Japanese cars in the Soviet market. However, due to various economic and political problems, the Moskvitch-2141 suffered from low quality, reliability and availability issues and was later replaced by the 2141-02 Svyatogor and the M-2142 sedan in the late 1990s.

entries.EN:
A 4x4 off-road vehicle developed as a replacement for the GAZ-69, the UAZ 469 is powered by a 2.5-liter inline-four petrol engine that produces 75 horsepower and 167 Nm of torque with a top speed of 100 km/h (62 mph). The UAZ 469 is known for its ruggedness, simplicity, and reliability and can traverse almost any terrain. The vehicle is widely used by the military, police and emergency services, as well as by civilians and off-road enthusiasts.

entries.EN:
A small city car based on the Fiat 600, the ZAZ 965 is powered by a 0.7-liter V4 air-cooled engine that produces 23 horsepower and 39 Nm of torque with a top speed of 90 km/h (56 mph). The ZAZ 965 is known for its distinctive appearance and was nicknamed “Zaporozhets” by the Soviet people, meaning “a person from Zaporizhia”, the city where the ZAZ factory is located. The ZAZ 965 was popular among the Soviet working class, as it was affordable, easy to maintain and suitable for urban driving.
